content.title: About
content.content: Barbecue chicken consists of chicken pieces marinated in spices and barbecue sauce, then baked or grilled. The meat becomes aromatic, slightly sweet, and coated with a caramelized crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Barbecue originated in the United States, where meat was cooked over an open flame.
Chicken in barbecue sauce often carries smoky notes obtained with liquid smoke or actual smoking.
There are many regional barbecue sauce styles, from sweet tomato‑based to tangy vinegar‑based.
Chicken cooks faster than beef, making barbecue chicken a popular quick family dinner.
The combination of lean protein and spices provides a flavorful source of energy.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, chicken, especially skinless breast, contains less saturated fat.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Barbecue chicken supplies B3 (niacin) and B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken is a source of phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Spices in the sauce (paprika, garlic, onion) have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Undercooking risk
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked to avoid food‑borne illnesses such as salmonella.

items.title: Sugar in sauce
items.content: Barbecue sauce often contains added sugar, increasing calories and affecting blood glucose.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to sauce ingredients like mustard or vinegar.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces can be salty; those monitoring sodium should choose low‑salt versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Barbecue chicken can be served as a main dish, sliced into salads, used in sandwiches, tacos, or as a pizza topping. It pairs well with corn, potatoes, fresh vegetables, and light side sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked barbecue chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in freezer‑safe bags for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
